creators.why: Firewall turns a soft fabric into a depth-sensing interface people want to push their hands into.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、作曲家、创意技术人
creators.bio_zh: 美国媒体艺术家和作曲家（与 Kiori Kawai 组成 Purring Tiger），制作互动视听装置与演出，代表作《Firewall》是一张会对按压做出反应的弹力布幕。
creators.why_zh: 《Firewall》把一块柔软的布变成人们忍不住想把手按进去的深度感应界面。

creators.name: Rebecca Horn
creators.role: Artist; performance, body extensions and kinetic sculpture
creators.bio: German artist (1944–2024) who began with wearable 'body extensions' that stretched the senses and moved on to feathered, motorised sculptures and room-sized machines that seem to breathe, paint and play.
creators.why: She treated the body as an interface to be extended and the machine as a performer, which is exactly the space where wearable AR lives.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；表演、身体延伸装置与动态雕塑
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家（1944–2024），早期以可穿戴的“身体延伸”作品拓展感官，后来创作带羽毛的电动雕塑和能“呼吸”、绘画、演奏的房间尺度机器。
creators.why_zh: 她把身体当作可以延伸的界面、把机器当作表演者，这正是可穿戴 AR 所处的空间。
creators.based_zh: 柏林，德国 / 巴黎，法国

creators.name: Jesús Rafael Soto
creators.role: Artist; kinetic and op art pioneer
creators.bio: Venezuelan artist (1923–2005) of the Paris kinetic movement, known for 'Vibrations' that shimmer as you move and for 'Penetrables', rooms of hanging threads or tubes that visitors walk through.
creators.why: His works only exist through the viewer's motion and body, a direct lesson for parallax, occlusion and walk-through volumes in AR.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；动态艺术与欧普艺术先驱
creators.bio_zh: 委内瑞拉艺术家（1923–2005），巴黎动态艺术运动的核心人物，以随观者移动而颤动的“振动”系列和可以走进去的悬挂线管空间“可穿透体”（Penetrables）闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品只有在观者移动、身体进入时才成立，对 AR 中的视差、遮挡和可穿行体积是直接的启发。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 加拉加斯，委内瑞拉

creators.name: Julio Le Parc
creators.role: Artist; light and kinetic art, co-founder of GRAV
creators.bio: Argentine artist (born 1928) and co-founder of GRAV (Groupe de Recherche d'Art Visuel), who since the late 1950s has built mobiles of reflective plates, moving-light rooms and games that turn spectators into participants.
creators.why: He made light itself move through space and insisted the viewer complete the work, two principles at the heart of AR design.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；光与动态艺术，GRAV 视觉艺术研究小组联合创始人
creators.bio_zh: 阿根廷艺术家（生于 1928 年），GRAV（视觉艺术研究小组）联合创始人。自 1950 年代末起创作反光片组成的“连续运动”装置、流动光影房间和让观众参与的游戏。
creators.why_zh: 他让光本身在空间里流动，并坚持由观众完成作品，这两点正是 AR 设计的核心。

creators.name: Carlos Cruz-Diez
creators.role: Artist; researcher of colour as an event
creators.bio: Venezuelan artist (1923–2019) who treated colour as something that happens in real time and space, through series such as Physichromie, Transchromie, Chromointerference and the walk-in colour rooms of Chromosaturation.
creators.why: He showed that colour can change with the viewer's position and time, which is a model for view-dependent materials and colour overlays in AR.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；把色彩当作“事件”来研究
creators.bio_zh: 委内瑞拉艺术家（1923–2019），把色彩视为在时间和空间中实时发生的现象，代表系列包括 Physichromie、Transchromie、Chromointerference，以及可以走进去的色彩房间 Chromosaturation。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了颜色会随观者位置和时间而变化，这是 AR 中视角相关材质与色彩叠加的范本。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 加拉加斯，委内瑞拉

creators.name: Otto Piene
creators.role: Artist; co-founder of ZERO, pioneer of light and sky art
creators.bio: German artist (1928–2014), co-founder of the ZERO group and later director of MIT's Center for Advanced Visual Studies, who made rotating perforated lamps flood rooms with moving light ('Lichtballett') and later inflatable sky sculptures.
creators.why: His light ballets turn a whole room into a moving display using only a lamp and a perforated shell, a lesson in cheap, spatial light effects.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；ZERO 小组联合创始人，光艺术与天空艺术先驱
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家（1928–2014），ZERO 小组联合创始人，后任 MIT 高级视觉研究中心主任。他用旋转的穿孔灯让整个房间充满流动的光点（“光之芭蕾”），后来又创作充气天空雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他的光之芭蕾只用一盏灯和一个穿孔外壳就把整个房间变成运动的屏幕，是低成本空间光效的范例。
creators.based_zh: 杜塞尔多夫，德国 / 剑桥，美国

creators.name: Nam June Paik (白南准)
creators.role: Artist; founder of video art
creators.based: New York, US / Seoul, South Korea
creators.bio: Korean-American artist (1932–2006) of Fluxus who turned television into a sculptural, playable material: magnets bending the picture, TVs growing in a garden, a Buddha watching himself on a closed circuit, robots and TV cellos in performance.
creators.why: He was the first to treat the screen as a physical object in space that the audience can touch and distort, the conceptual root of screen-in-the-world AR.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；录像艺术之父
creators.bio_zh: 韩裔美国艺术家（1932–2006），激浪派成员，把电视变成可雕塑、可玩的材料：用磁铁扭曲画面、让电视在花园里生长、让佛像在闭路电视里看自己，还有机器人和电视大提琴表演。
creators.why_zh: 他最早把屏幕当作空间中的物体，让观众可以触碰和扭曲它，这是“屏幕进入现实世界”式 AR 的概念源头。
creators.based_zh: 纽约，美国 / 首尔，韩国

creators.name: Nicolas Schöffer
creators.role: Artist; father of cybernetic art
creators.bio: Hungarian-born French artist (1912–1992) who built 'spatiodynamic' sculptures of polished metal, motors and light, including CYSP 1 (1956), the first sculpture to react autonomously to sound, light and movement, and a 52 m cybernetic light tower in Liège.
creators.why: He was the first to give a sculpture sensors and behaviour, the same loop of sensing and responding that drives interactive AR content.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；控制论艺术之父
creators.bio_zh: 匈牙利裔法国艺术家（1912–1992），用抛光金属、电机和灯光制作“空间动力”雕塑。1956 年的 CYSP 1 是第一件能自主响应声音、光和运动的雕塑，他还在列日建造了 52 米高的控制论光塔。
creators.why_zh: 他最早给雕塑装上传感器和行为逻辑，这正是驱动交互式 AR 内容的“感知—回应”循环。

creators.name: Edward Ihnatowicz
creators.role: Artist; pioneer of robotic and cybernetic sculpture
creators.bio: Polish-born British sculptor (1926–1988) whose Senster (1970), a 4 m hydraulic creature at Philips' Evoluon, turned toward quiet sounds and slow movement, and whose SAM (1968) leaned toward voices at Cybernetic Serendipity.
creators.why: He proved that a few sensors and simple rules can give an object a believable personality, a key idea for AR characters that notice people.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；机器人与控制论雕塑先驱
creators.bio_zh: 波兰裔英国雕塑家（1926–1988）。他的 Senster（1970）是陈列在飞利浦 Evoluon 的 4 米液压“生物”，会转向轻柔的声音和缓慢的动作；SAM（1968）则在“控制论的偶然”展上向说话的人探身。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了几个传感器加简单规则就能让物体拥有可信的个性，这是会“注意到人”的 AR 角色的关键思路。

creators.name: Jean Tinguely
creators.role: Artist; maker of absurd kinetic machines
creators.bio: Swiss artist (1925–1991) who built noisy, self-destroying and drawing machines from scrap, from the Méta-Matic drawing robots (1959) and Homage to New York (1960) to the forest giant Le Cyclop.
creators.why: His machines make process, noise and failure the spectacle, a reminder that visible mechanics and chance can be more engaging than polish.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；荒诞动态机器的制造者
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士艺术家（1925–1991），用废旧零件制造吵闹、会自毁、会画画的机器，从 Méta-Matic 绘画机器（1959）、《向纽约致敬》（1960）到森林中的巨型雕塑 Le Cyclop。
creators.why_zh: 他的机器把过程、噪音和失败本身变成奇观，提醒我们：可见的机制与偶然性往往比精致更吸引人。
creators.based_zh: 巴塞尔，瑞士 / 巴黎，法国

creators.name: Alexander Calder
creators.role: Artist; inventor of the mobile
creators.bio: American sculptor (1898–1976) who invented the mobile, balanced abstract shapes that move with air and touch, and who performed his wire Cirque Calder by hand.
creators.why: His mobiles show how a few balanced parts can create endless motion, a model for physics-driven, ambient AR objects.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；“动态雕塑”（mobile）的发明者
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家（1898–1976），发明了随空气与触碰而运动的平衡抽象雕塑“mobile”，还亲手表演铁丝马戏团 Cirque Calder。
creators.why_zh: 他的动态雕塑说明几个平衡的部件就能产生无穷的运动，是基于物理、营造氛围的 AR 物体的范本。
creators.based_zh: 罗克斯伯里，美国 / 萨谢，法国

creators.name: George Rickey
creators.role: Artist; kinetic sculptor of wind-driven blades
creators.bio: American sculptor (1907–2002) whose stainless-steel blades, lines and planes, balanced on precise bearings, swing and gyrate slowly in the slightest wind.
creators.why: He choreographed air with engineering alone, a lesson for AR objects that respond to wind, breath or device motion with calm, readable movement.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；风动不锈钢叶片的动态雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家（1907–2002），他的不锈钢叶片、线条和平面装在精密轴承上，在最轻的风中缓慢摆动、旋转。
creators.why_zh: 他只靠工程就编排了空气的舞蹈，启发 AR 物体以平静、易读的运动回应风、呼吸或手机的晃动。

creators.name: Len Lye
creators.role: Artist; kinetic sculptor and experimental filmmaker
creators.based: New York, US / New Plymouth, New Zealand
creators.bio: New Zealand-born artist (1901–1980) who painted directly on film and built 'tangible motion sculptures' of flexing steel that whip, sing and shimmer; many were realised full size after his death by the Len Lye Foundation.
creators.why: He treated motion as the material itself, which is how AR designers should think about animation in space.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；动态雕塑家与实验电影人
creators.bio_zh: 新西兰出生的艺术家（1901–1980），直接在胶片上作画，也制作会甩动、鸣响、闪烁的弹性钢“可触的运动雕塑”；许多作品在他去世后由 Len Lye 基金会按原尺寸实现。
creators.why_zh: 他把运动本身当作材料，这正是 AR 设计师看待空间动画的方式。
creators.based_zh: 纽约，美国 / 新普利茅斯，新西兰

creators.name: Takis
creators.role: Artist; sculptor of magnetism, light and sound
creators.bio: Greek artist Panayiotis Vassilakis (1925–2019) who made invisible forces visible: objects floating on magnetic fields, blinking 'Signaux' (signals) on tall rods, and musical sculptures played by magnets.
creators.why: He made invisible fields tangible, the same job AR does when it shows sensor data, forces or signals in space.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；以磁力、光和声音创作的雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 希腊艺术家帕纳约蒂斯·瓦西拉基斯（Takis，1925–2019），让看不见的力显形：悬浮在磁场中的物体、高杆上闪烁的“信号”（Signaux），以及由磁铁演奏的音乐雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他让看不见的场变得可感知，这正是 AR 在空间中显示传感器数据、力或信号时所做的事。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 雅典，希腊

creators.name: Pol Bury
creators.role: Artist; sculptor of slow kinetic movement
creators.bio: Belgian artist (1922–2005) who made movement almost imperceptible: balls and rods that creep on hidden motors, and polished steel fountains whose spheres tip and pour water in slow rhythms.
creators.why: He showed that slowness can be more captivating than speed, a useful lesson for calm, ambient AR animation.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；慢速动态雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 比利时艺术家（1922–2005），让运动几乎难以察觉：由隐藏电机缓慢推动的球和杆，以及抛光不锈钢球体慢慢倾斜、倒水的喷泉。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了慢比快更能吸引人，对平静、氛围型的 AR 动画很有启发。

creators.name: László Moholy-Nagy
creators.role: Artist; Bauhaus teacher and pioneer of light art
creators.bio: Hungarian artist (1895–1946) and Bauhaus teacher who built the Light Prop for an Electric Stage (1930), a motorised machine of metal and glass that throws moving shadows and reflections around a room, and filmed it as Ein Lichtspiel Schwarz Weiss Grau.
creators.why: He treated light and shadow as a spatial medium a century before AR, and imagined rooms that are made of projected light.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；包豪斯教师，光艺术先驱
creators.bio_zh: 匈牙利艺术家（1895–1946），包豪斯教师。他制作的《电动舞台光道具》（1930）是一台由金属和玻璃组成的电动机器，把移动的光影和反射投满整个房间，并拍成电影《光的游戏：黑白灰》。
creators.why_zh: 他在 AR 出现前一个世纪就把光与影当作空间媒介，设想由投射光构成的房间。
creators.based_zh: 柏林，德国 / 芝加哥，美国

creators.name: Gianni Colombo
creators.role: Artist; kinetic and programmed-art pioneer, member of Gruppo T
creators.bio: Italian artist (1937–1993) of Milan's Gruppo T who built pulsating reliefs and 'programmed environments' such as Spazio elastico (1967), a dark room of fluorescent elastic cords that slowly stretch and shift under UV light.
creators.why: His environments deform the space around the body instead of showing an image, a lesson in spatial, full-room AR effects.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；动态与程序艺术先驱，T 小组成员
creators.bio_zh: 意大利艺术家（1937–1993），米兰 T 小组（Gruppo T）成员，创作会脉动的浮雕和“程序化环境”，例如《弹性空间》（1967）：黑暗房间里荧光弹性绳在紫外光下缓慢拉伸、移位。
creators.why_zh: 他的环境不是展示图像，而是让身体周围的空间本身变形，这是全房间 AR 效果的一课。

creators.name: Eadweard Muybridge
creators.role: Photographer; pioneer of motion photography (1830–1904)
creators.based: San Francisco and Philadelphia, US (born Kingston upon Thames, UK)
creators.bio: English-born photographer who used banks of tripwire-triggered cameras to split a galloping horse, athletes and animals into sequences of still frames, then projected them as moving images with his zoopraxiscope.
creators.why: He turned one invisible instant of motion into a row of frames you can walk along — the founding gesture of every motion trail and onion-skin in AR.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师；运动摄影先驱（1830–1904）
creators.bio_zh: 出生于英国的摄影师，用一排由绊线触发的相机把奔马、运动员和动物的动作拆成连续的静帧，再用自制的 zoopraxiscope 把它们投影成活动影像。
creators.why_zh: 他把看不见的一瞬运动切成一排可以沿着走过去看的画面——这是 AR 里所有运动残影和洋葱皮效果的起点。
creators.based_zh: 美国旧金山与费城（生于英国泰晤士河畔金斯顿）

creators.name: Étienne-Jules Marey
creators.role: Physiologist and inventor of chronophotography (1830–1904)
creators.bio: French physiologist who built the chronophotographic gun, fixed-plate chronophotography, bronze and plaster zoetrope sculptures of birds in flight, and smoke machines that made air currents visible.
creators.why: Marey drew motion as a single layered image and even as a physical sculpture — a direct model for turning tracked movement into 3D forms in AR.
creators.role_zh: 生理学家、连续摄影（chronophotography）的发明者（1830–1904）
creators.bio_zh: 法国生理学家，发明了连续摄影枪和单底片连续摄影，制作过鸟类飞行的石膏与青铜走马盘雕塑，还造出让气流显形的烟雾机。
creators.why_zh: Marey 把运动画成一张叠加的图像，甚至做成实体雕塑——这正是在 AR 中把追踪到的动作变成三维形体的直接范本。

creators.name: Harold "Doc" Edgerton
creators.role: Electrical engineer, MIT professor, father of stroboscopic photography (1903–1990)
creators.bio: MIT engineer who developed the electronic stroboscope and microsecond flash, freezing milk drops, bullets and athletes and layering multiple flashes into a single frame.
creators.why: Edgerton showed that a controlled flash of light can cut time into slices — the same trick behind strobe-based persistence effects in AR and 3D zoetropes.
creators.role_zh: 电气工程师、MIT 教授、频闪摄影之父（1903–1990）
creators.bio_zh: MIT 工程师，发明了电子频闪仪和微秒级闪光，定格了牛奶滴、子弹和运动员，也把多次闪光叠进同一张画面。
creators.why_zh: Edgerton 证明了一道受控的闪光就能把时间切成薄片——AR 中基于频闪的残影效果和 3D 走马盘用的正是同一招。

creators.name: Gjon Mili
creators.role: Photographer and filmmaker, LIFE magazine (1904–1984)
creators.bio: Albanian-American photographer who worked with Harold Edgerton on stroboscopic and multiple-flash photography and, in 1949, photographed Pablo Picasso drawing in the air with a small light.
creators.why: His Picasso light drawings are the most famous proof that a gesture in empty air can become a lasting drawing — the core idea of every AR air-drawing tool.
creators.role_zh: LIFE 杂志摄影师与电影人（1904–1984）
creators.bio_zh: 阿尔巴尼亚裔美国摄影师，曾与 Harold Edgerton 一起研究频闪和多次闪光摄影；1949 年他拍下了 Pablo Picasso 用小手电在空中作画的照片。
creators.why_zh: 他拍的 Picasso 光绘最有力地证明了：在空中的一个手势也能变成留下来的画——这正是所有 AR 空中绘画工具的核心。
creators.based_zh: 美国纽约（生于阿尔巴尼亚科尔察）

creators.name: Frank & Lillian Gilbreth
creators.role: Industrial engineers; inventors of the cyclegraph and chronocyclegraph
creators.bio: American engineers and time-and-motion researchers who fixed small lights to workers' hands and photographed them with long exposures, producing light traces of movement and wire sculptures of the ideal motion path.
creators.why: Their cyclegraphs were the first light paintings made for analysis: motion turned into a 3D line you can study — exactly what AR hand tracking can now draw live.
creators.role_zh: 工业工程师；光迹摄影（cyclegraph）和计时光迹摄影（chronocyclegraph）的发明者
creators.bio_zh: 美国工程师和动作研究者，把小灯绑在工人手上用长曝光拍摄，得到动作的光迹，并据此弯出表示“理想动作路径”的铁丝雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他们的光迹照片是最早为分析而做的光绘：把动作变成一条可以研究的三维线——这正是今天 AR 手部追踪可以实时画出来的东西。
creators.based_zh: 美国新泽西州蒙特克莱尔

creators.name: Eric Staller
creators.role: Light artist and designer
creators.bio: American artist known for 1970s 'Lightscapes' light-drawing photographs in New York streets and for public light works such as the Lightmobile, a Volkswagen Beetle covered in computer-controlled bulbs.
creators.why: He carried light drawing out of the studio into the street and onto moving objects — a reminder that AR content can ride on vehicles and people, not just stay on tables.
creators.role_zh: 光艺术家与设计师
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以 1970 年代在纽约街头拍摄的光绘作品《Lightscapes》，以及布满电脑控制灯泡的甲壳虫汽车《Lightmobile》等公共光艺术闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他把光绘从工作室带到街头、带到移动的物体上——提醒我们 AR 内容也可以跟着车和人走，而不只停在桌面上。
creators.based_zh: 荷兰阿姆斯特丹（生于美国纽约）

creators.name: Lichtfaktor
creators.role: Light-painting and light-graffiti collective
creators.bio: Cologne collective (Marcel Panne, Jan Leonardo Wöllert and friends) who since 2006 have made light-graffiti photographs and stop-motion films drawn frame by frame with flashlights, plus interactive light-painting setups for festivals.
creators.why: Lichtfaktor animates long-exposure drawings frame by frame, showing how hand-drawn light can live in real streets — the look many AR drawing apps try to reproduce live.
creators.role_zh: 光绘与光涂鸦团体
creators.bio_zh: 科隆的光绘团体（Marcel Panne、Jan Leonardo Wöllert 等），自 2006 年起用手电逐帧绘制光涂鸦照片和定格动画，也为艺术节做互动光绘装置。
creators.why_zh: Lichtfaktor 把长曝光光绘一帧一帧地做成动画，让手绘的光在真实街道里活起来——这正是许多 AR 绘画应用想实时做到的效果。

creators.name: Darren Pearson (DARIUSTWIN)
creators.role: Light-painting artist and animator
creators.bio: Los Angeles artist who draws glowing skeletons, dinosaurs and characters in the air with handheld lights and strings hundreds of long exposures into light-painting stop-motion films.
creators.why: His characters exist only as light traces placed in real landscapes — a hand-made version of AR characters anchored in the world.
creators.role_zh: 光绘艺术家与动画师
creators.bio_zh: 洛杉矶艺术家，用手持光源在空中画出发光的骷髅、恐龙和角色，再把几百张长曝光照片串成光绘定格动画。
creators.why_zh: 他的角色只以光迹的形式存在于真实风景中——就像手工做出来的、锚定在现实世界里的 AR 角色。

creators.name: Stephen Wilkes
creators.role: Photographer
creators.bio: American photographer whose 'Day to Night' series stitches up to 1,500 frames shot from one fixed position over 15 to 30 hours into a single image that flows from daylight to night.
creators.why: He shows time as a gradient across space in one picture — a strong model for AR views that let you scrub time by moving through a place.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师
creators.bio_zh: 美国摄影师，他的《Day to Night》系列在同一机位连续拍摄 15 到 30 小时、最多 1500 张照片，再合成一张从白天过渡到夜晚的画面。
creators.why_zh: 他在一张照片里把时间铺成空间上的渐变——这对“走动就能拖动时间轴”的 AR 视图是很好的范本。
creators.based_zh: 美国康涅狄格州韦斯特波特

creators.name: BERG (Jack Schulze, Matt Webb, Timo Arnall)
creators.role: Design consultancy (2005–2014)
creators.bio: London design studio known for Little Printer, the 'Media Surfaces' films and experiments that made invisible technology visible, often with Timo Arnall's film work.
creators.why: BERG treated screens, networks and light as materials in physical space, a design stance that anticipated much of today's spatial computing.
creators.bio_zh: 伦敦设计工作室，以 Little Printer、《Media Surfaces》系列短片，以及让看不见的技术显形的实验闻名，许多影片由 Timo Arnall 拍摄。
creators.why_zh: BERG 把屏幕、网络和光都当作物理空间里的材料，这种设计立场预示了今天空间计算的许多方向。

creators.name: Timo Arnall
creators.role: Designer and filmmaker; Immaterials project
creators.bio: Designer and filmmaker who, with Jørn Knutsen and Einar Sneve Martinussen at the Oslo School of Architecture and Design, made the 'Immaterials' films that visualise RFID fields and WiFi signal strength with long-exposure light.
creators.why: Immaterials is the reference for making invisible data fields visible in real space — exactly what AR data overlays try to do.
creators.role_zh: 设计师与电影人；Immaterials 项目
creators.bio_zh: 设计师与电影人，与奥斯陆建筑与设计学院的 Jørn Knutsen、Einar Sneve Martinussen 合作拍摄了《Immaterials》系列，用长曝光的光把 RFID 场和 WiFi 信号强度画出来。
creators.why_zh: 《Immaterials》是“让看不见的数据场在真实空间里显形”的标杆——这正是 AR 数据叠加想做的事。
creators.based_zh: 挪威奥斯陆 / 英国伦敦

creators.name: Hiroshi Sugimoto (杉本博司)
creators.role: Photographer and architect
creators.based: Tokyo, Japan and New York, US
creators.bio: Japanese artist whose 'Theaters' expose one photograph for the full length of a film, leaving a glowing white screen, and whose 'Seascapes' repeat one horizon of sea and sky across the world.
creators.why: His long exposures show that a camera can collapse hours into one frame — a way to think about AR that shows accumulated time instead of the present moment.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师、建筑师
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家。他的《Theaters》系列让一张底片曝光整部电影的时长，只留下发光的白色银幕；《Seascapes》系列在世界各地重复拍摄同一种海天之间的地平线。
creators.why_zh: 他的长曝光说明相机可以把几个小时压进一帧——让人思考 AR 不只显示此刻，也可以显示累积的时间。

creators.name: Norman McLaren
creators.role: Animator and filmmaker, National Film Board of Canada (1914–1987)
creators.bio: Scottish-Canadian animator at the NFB who painted directly on film, invented pixilation with live actors, and used optical printing to multiply dancers into trails of motion.
creators.why: McLaren treated time as a material you can print, stretch and repeat — the same levers AR designers use for echoes, trails and slow motion.
creators.role_zh: 加拿大国家电影局动画师与导演（1914–1987）
creators.bio_zh: 苏格兰裔加拿大动画师，在加拿大国家电影局（NFB）工作。他直接在胶片上作画，发明了用真人拍的“逐格真人动画”（pixilation），还用光学印片把舞者复制成一串运动轨迹。
creators.why_zh: McLaren 把时间当成可以印制、拉伸和重复的材料——AR 设计师做回声、拖尾和慢动作用的也是这些手段。
creators.based_zh: 加拿大蒙特利尔（生于苏格兰斯特灵）

creators.name: Adam Magyar
creators.role: Photographer and video artist
creators.bio: Hungarian artist who adapts industrial line-scan and high-speed cameras to record city crowds: 'Urban Flow' slit-scan panoramas of pedestrians and 'Stainless' ultra-slow films of commuters on passing subway platforms.
creators.why: His custom cameras show that changing how a sensor samples time produces a completely new picture of the same street — a lesson for AR camera effects.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师、影像艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 匈牙利艺术家，改装工业线扫描相机和高速摄影机来记录城市人群：《Urban Flow》用狭缝扫描拍下行人全景，《Stainless》用超慢速影像拍下列车驶过站台时的乘客。
creators.why_zh: 他的改装相机说明：只要改变传感器对时间的采样方式，同一条街就会变成全新的画面——这对 AR 相机特效很有启发。

creators.name: Zbigniew Rybczyński
creators.role: Filmmaker and video pioneer
creators.bio: Polish filmmaker and Academy Award winner whose 'Tango' layers 36 looping characters in one room, and who pioneered HD video compositing and slit-scan time effects in 'Steps' and 'The Fourth Dimension'.
creators.why: Tango is the clearest demonstration of many time loops sharing one space without colliding — a direct model for layering recorded people in AR.
creators.role_zh: 导演、录像艺术先驱
creators.bio_zh: 波兰导演、奥斯卡奖得主。《Tango》把 36 个循环动作的人物叠在同一个房间里；他还在《Steps》和《The Fourth Dimension》中开创了高清视频合成和狭缝扫描式的时间特效。
creators.why_zh: 《Tango》最清楚地展示了许多时间循环如何共享同一空间而互不碰撞——这是在 AR 里叠放录下来的人的直接范本。

creators.name: Michael Wesely
creators.role: Photographer
creators.bio: German photographer who builds pinhole-like cameras with extremely long exposures, recording construction sites such as Potsdamer Platz in Berlin and the Museum of Modern Art in New York over two to three years in a single image.
creators.why: His years-long exposures show a building rising as a ghostly overlay of its own history — the look of an AR 'time layer' over a site.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师
creators.bio_zh: 德国摄影师，自制超长曝光相机，在一张照片里记录柏林波茨坦广场、纽约现代艺术博物馆等工地两三年的变化。
creators.why_zh: 他长达数年的曝光让建筑在自身历史的幽灵般叠影中长出来——这就是 AR 叠加在场地上的“时间图层”应有的样子。

creators.name: Antony Gormley
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: British sculptor who casts his own body in iron and steel and places the figures on beaches, rooftops, mountains and salt lakes, from Another Place to the Angel of the North.
creators.why: He shows that a single human figure placed in a landscape turns the whole place into a stage and changes how every passer-by reads it.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 英国雕塑家，用自己的身体翻模铸成铁或钢的人像，把它们安放在海滩、屋顶、山坡和盐湖上，代表作有《Another Place》和《Angel of the North》。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了：把一个人形放进风景里，整个地方就变成了舞台，每个路人对它的理解都会随之改变。

creators.name: Xavi Bou
creators.role: Photographer and visual artist
creators.bio: Barcelona photographer trained in geology who, since 2012, stacks video frames of birds in flight into single images (Ornithographies) that reveal the shapes their paths draw in the sky.
creators.why: His digital chronophotography is the clearest model for AR trails: it makes an invisible path in the real sky visible without changing the sky.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师、视觉艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 出身地质学的巴塞罗那摄影师，自 2012 年起把飞鸟视频的连续帧叠合成一张图像（Ornithographies），让鸟在天空中画出的轨迹显形。
creators.why_zh: 他的数字连续摄影是 AR 轨迹效果最清楚的范本：不改变天空，只让真实天空中看不见的路径显形。

creators.name: Andy Goldsworthy
creators.role: Land artist and sculptor
creators.bio: British artist who works with leaves, ice, stone, wood and the tide, making both ephemeral pieces that melt or wash away and permanent walls and cairns.
creators.why: His work teaches that time, weather and decay can be part of a piece, which is exactly what a persistent, site-anchored AR work has to design for.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家、雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，用树叶、冰、石头、木头和潮水创作，既有会融化、被冲走的短暂作品，也有长期存在的石墙和石堆。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品说明时间、天气和衰败都可以成为作品的一部分，这正是长期锚定在某地的 AR 作品需要设计的东西。

creators.name: Christo and Jeanne-Claude
creators.role: Environmental artists
creators.bio: Artist couple who wrapped buildings and coastlines in fabric and ran fences, curtains, gates and floating piers across landscapes for two or three weeks at a time, financing every project themselves.
creators.why: They proved that a temporary layer laid over a familiar place makes people see its true shape, the core promise of AR overlays.
creators.role_zh: 环境艺术家二人组
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家夫妇，用织物包裹建筑和海岸，在风景中架设围栏、帘幕、门廊和浮桥，每件作品只存在两三周，全部自筹资金完成。
creators.why_zh: 他们证明了：在熟悉的地方覆盖一层临时的表层，反而让人看清它原本的形状，这正是 AR 叠加的核心承诺。

creators.name: Robert Smithson
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: American artist (1938–1973) and founding figure of Land Art, best known for Spiral Jetty, a 457-metre coil of basalt in Utah's Great Salt Lake.
creators.why: He made scale, entropy and the view from the air part of the artwork, a vocabulary AR designers reuse for world-scale content.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家（1938–1973），大地艺术的奠基人之一，代表作是犹他州大盐湖中长 457 米的玄武岩螺旋《Spiral Jetty》。
creators.why_zh: 他把尺度、熵和空中视角纳入作品，这套语汇正是 AR 设计世界尺度内容时要借用的。

creators.name: Nancy Holt
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: American artist (1938–2014) whose concrete tunnels, rings and pipes frame the sun, stars and horizon at precise moments such as the solstices.
creators.why: Her works are physical viewfinders aligned to the sky, the same logic as an AR anchor that only resolves from one place at one time.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家（1938–2014），她用混凝土隧道、圆环和管道在特定时刻（如至日）精确框住太阳、星星和地平线。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品是对准天空的实体取景器，与只在某个地点、某个时刻才成立的 AR 锚点逻辑相同。
creators.based_zh: 纽约 / 新墨西哥，美国

creators.name: Walter De Maria
creators.role: Sculptor and land artist
creators.bio: American artist (1935–2013) known for The Lightning Field, 400 steel poles on a grid in the New Mexico desert, and for rooms filled with earth.
creators.why: He turned a measured grid into a device for watching light, weather and time, a lesson in how few elements an augmented landscape needs.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家、大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家（1935–2013），以新墨西哥沙漠中 400 根不锈钢杆组成的网格《The Lightning Field》和装满泥土的房间闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他把精确测量的网格变成观看光、天气和时间的装置，说明增强一片风景只需要极少的元素。

creators.name: Richard Long
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: British artist who since 1967 has made art by walking: lines trodden into grass, stone circles and text works that record routes across the world.
creators.why: A Line Made by Walking is the first 'trace' artwork: the body's path becomes the drawing, exactly what location-based AR records.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，自 1967 年起以行走为创作：在草地上踩出线条，摆放石圈，并用文字记录他走过的世界各地路线。
creators.why_zh: 《A Line Made by Walking》是最早的“痕迹”作品之一：身体的路径就是绘画，这正是基于位置的 AR 所记录的东西。

creators.name: Michael Heizer
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: American artist who cuts and moves the desert at monumental scale: Double Negative, Levitated Mass and City, a mile-long complex he built in Nevada over five decades.
creators.why: His negative spaces and suspended boulder show how absence and implied danger can be designed, useful for AR that subtracts rather than adds.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以巨大尺度切割和搬运沙漠：《Double Negative》《Levitated Mass》，以及他在内华达用五十年建成、长约一英里的《City》。
creators.why_zh: 他的“负空间”和悬空巨石展示了如何设计缺失和隐含的危险感，对做减法而非加法的 AR 很有启发。

creators.name: Charles Ross
creators.role: Artist working with light and astronomy
creators.bio: American artist known for prisms and solar burns and for Star Axis, a naked-eye observatory carved into a New Mexico mesa and aligned with Earth's axis.
creators.why: Star Axis makes a 26,000-year cycle walkable, a model for AR that ties a physical path to astronomical data.
creators.role_zh: 以光与天文为材料的艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以棱镜和“太阳灼烧”作品闻名，代表作《Star Axis》是开凿在新墨西哥台地中、对准地轴的肉眼天文台。
creators.why_zh: 《Star Axis》让一个 26000 年的周期变得可以用脚走完，是把实体路径和天文数据绑定的 AR 范本。
creators.based_zh: 纽约 / 新墨西哥，美国

creators.name: Maya Lin
creators.role: Artist and architect
creators.bio: American artist and architect who designed the Vietnam Veterans Memorial as a student and makes earthworks and environmental memorials such as Wavefield and Ghost Forest.
creators.why: She shapes land and names so that information (lost lives, lost species) is felt by walking, an approach AR memorials can borrow.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、建筑师
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家、建筑师，学生时代设计了越战纪念碑，之后创作了《Wavefield》《Ghost Forest》等大地作品与环境纪念作品。
creators.why_zh: 她塑造土地和名字，让信息（逝去的生命、消失的物种）通过行走被感受到，这种方式值得 AR 纪念作品借鉴。

creators.name: Agnes Denes
creators.role: Conceptual and environmental artist
creators.bio: Hungarian-born American pioneer of ecological art who planted two acres of wheat on a Manhattan landfill in 1982 and a mountain of 11,000 trees in Finland.
creators.why: Her works put a living system into the wrong place to make a value system visible, a strong template for AR critique.
creators.role_zh: 观念艺术家、环境艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 出生于匈牙利的美国生态艺术先驱，1982 年在曼哈顿垃圾填埋地种下两英亩小麦，又在芬兰种出由 11000 棵树组成的山。
creators.why_zh: 她把一个活的系统放在“不该出现”的地方，让一套价值观显形，这是 AR 批判性作品的有力模板。

creators.name: Chris Drury
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: British artist who builds stone and turf 'cloud chambers', camera obscuras that project the sky onto the floor, and earthworks based on patterns of weather, water and the body.
creators.why: His cloud chambers are pre-digital passthrough: a dark room that shows the outside world live, the ancestor of the AR viewport.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，用石头和草皮建造“云室”（把天空投到地面上的暗箱），并以天气、水和人体的纹样创作大地作品。
creators.why_zh: 他的云室是前数字时代的“透视”：一间暗室实时呈现外面的世界，是 AR 取景窗的祖先。

creators.name: Doug Aitken
creators.role: Artist and filmmaker
creators.bio: American artist whose mirrored house (Mirage), mirrored hot-air balloon (New Horizon) and underwater pavilions dissolve architecture into the landscape it reflects.
creators.why: Mirrored volumes act like real-world shaders: the object is only the landscape, reframed, which is a clean idea for AR materials.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、电影人
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，他的镜面房屋《Mirage》、镜面热气球《New Horizon》和水下展亭让建筑消融在它所映照的风景里。
creators.why_zh: 镜面体块就像现实世界里的着色器：物体本身只是被重新框取的风景，这是 AR 材质设计的简洁思路。

creators.name: Tomás Saraceno
creators.role: Artist and architect
creators.bio: Argentine artist who builds cloud-like modules, walkable nets and Aerocene, a community of solar-powered balloons that fly without fossil fuels.
creators.why: He treats air, spiders' webs and the sky as shared media, a useful frame for multi-user AR that lives in the air above us.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、建筑师
creators.bio_zh: 阿根廷艺术家，创作云状模块、可行走的网，以及 Aerocene：一个不用化石燃料、仅靠太阳加热升空的气球社群项目。
creators.why_zh: 他把空气、蛛网和天空当作共享媒介，这对漂浮在头顶的多人 AR 很有参考价值。

creators.name: Jaume Plensa
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: Spanish sculptor of monumental heads made of letters, mesh or white stone, placed in plazas, parks and on the waterfront, including Chicago's Crown Fountain.
creators.why: His giant, eyes-closed faces show how a single calm figure can change the mood of a whole public space, a lesson for AR avatars in cities.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 西班牙雕塑家，以字母、网格或白色石材塑造巨大头像，安放在广场、公园和水岸，包括芝加哥的《Crown Fountain》。
creators.why_zh: 他那些闭着眼睛的巨大面孔说明，一个安静的形象就能改变整个公共空间的气氛，这是城市 AR 形象的一课。

creators.name: Anish Kapoor
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: British-Indian sculptor of mirror-polished and void-like forms such as Cloud Gate in Chicago, Sky Mirror and the whirlpool Descension.
creators.why: His reflective public works turn the sky and the crowd into the content of the sculpture, the same trick as environment-mapped AR objects.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 英籍印度裔雕塑家，以镜面抛光和“虚空”形态著称，如芝加哥的《Cloud Gate》《Sky Mirror》和漩涡作品《Descension》。
creators.why_zh: 他的镜面公共作品把天空和人群变成雕塑的内容，与使用环境贴图的 AR 物体是同一个把戏。

creators.name: Rob Mulholland
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: Scottish sculptor whose mirrored human figures stand in forests and lochs, reflecting their surroundings until they almost disappear.
creators.why: His mirror people are the physical version of an AR occlusion test: a figure that is present only through what it reflects.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 苏格兰雕塑家，他的镜面人形站在森林和湖中，映照周围环境，几乎消失不见。
creators.why_zh: 他的镜面人像是 AR 遮挡测试的实体版本：一个只通过反射才显现的人形。

creators.name: Saype (Guillaume Legros)
creators.role: Land artist and painter
creators.bio: French-Swiss artist who sprays giant figures onto grass with biodegradable paint made of chalk, charcoal and milk proteins; they fade as the grass grows.
creators.why: His paintings only resolve from the air or a distant slope, and they fade with time, two properties that location-based AR designers constantly deal with.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家、画家
creators.bio_zh: 法国与瑞士艺术家，用粉笔、木炭和牛奶蛋白制成的可降解颜料在草地上喷绘巨大人像，草长高后画面便会消失。
creators.why_zh: 他的画只有从空中或远处的坡上才看得完整，而且会随时间消退，这两点正是位置型 AR 设计者经常要处理的。

creators.name: Jim Denevan
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: American artist who draws enormous geometric patterns with a stick or rake on beaches, deserts and frozen lakes, including a nine-square-mile drawing on Lake Baikal.
creators.why: His drawings are made at walking height but only read from the air, a direct lesson in designing for two viewpoints at once.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，用木棍或耙子在海滩、沙漠和冰冻湖面上画出巨大的几何图案，包括在贝加尔湖冰面上面积达九平方英里的作品。
creators.why_zh: 他的画在步行高度完成，却只能从空中读懂，直接说明了如何同时为两种视点设计。
creators.based_zh: 圣克鲁兹，加利福尼亚，美国

creators.name: Andres Amador
creators.role: Sand artist
creators.bio: American artist who rakes vast geometric and organic patterns into beaches at low tide, knowing the sea will erase them within hours.
creators.why: His tide-bound drawings make impermanence a feature, and his group mandalas show how many people can co-draw one large image.
creators.role_zh: 沙画艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，在退潮的沙滩上耙出巨大的几何与有机图案，明知几小时后海水就会把它们抹去。
creators.why_zh: 他受潮汐限定的沙画把短暂变成了特色，他的集体曼陀罗也展示了多人如何共同画出一张巨图。

creators.name: Zadok Ben-David
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: Yemen-born, London-based sculptor known for fields of thousands of tiny etched-steel figures and flowers whose look changes completely as you walk around them.
creators.why: His two-sided fields show how the same objects can tell two stories depending on the viewer's position, a core AR idea.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 出生于也门、定居伦敦的雕塑家，以成千上万个蚀刻钢片小人与小花组成的场域闻名，观者绕行时作品会完全变样。
creators.why_zh: 他的双面场域说明同一组物体会随观者位置讲出两个故事，这是 AR 的核心思路之一。

creators.name: Not Vital
creators.role: Sculptor and architect
creators.bio: Swiss artist who builds sculptural houses, towers and 'houses to watch the sunset' in remote places from Niger to Patagonia, and runs a sculpture park in the Engadin.
creators.why: His buildings exist mainly to frame one view or one moment of the day, a pure example of designing an experience around a place.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家、建筑师
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士艺术家，在从尼日尔到巴塔哥尼亚的偏远地方建造雕塑般的房屋、塔楼和“看日落的房子”，并在恩加丁经营一座雕塑公园。
creators.why_zh: 他的建筑主要是为了框住某个景色或一天中的某个时刻，是围绕地点设计体验的纯粹例子。

creators.name: Pierre Huyghe
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: French artist who builds living, self-running environments with animals, bacteria, plants and algorithms, such as Untilled and After ALife Ahead.
creators.why: He designs systems rather than objects, so the work keeps changing whether or not anyone watches, a model for persistent AR worlds.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，用动物、细菌、植物和算法搭建能自行运转的活环境，如《Untilled》和《After ALife Ahead》。
creators.why_zh: 他设计的是系统而非物体，作品无论有没有人看都在变化，是持久型 AR 世界的范本。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 圣地亚哥，智利

creators.name: Ai Weiwei (艾未未)
creators.role: Artist and activist
creators.bio: Chinese artist whose large public installations use everyday objects in huge numbers, from 100 million porcelain seeds to refugee life jackets wrapped around a concert hall.
creators.why: His works show how repeating one object thousands of times in a public place turns a statistic into something you can walk into.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、社会活动家
creators.bio_zh: 中国艺术家，他的大型公共装置大量使用日常物件，从一亿颗瓷制葵花籽到包裹音乐厅的难民救生衣。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品说明，把一个物件在公共空间里重复成千上万次，就能把一个统计数字变成可以走进去的东西。

creators.name: Theo Jansen
creators.role: Kinetic artist
creators.bio: Dutch artist who since 1990 has evolved Strandbeests, wind-powered walking creatures made of PVC tubes that roam the beaches of the Netherlands.
creators.why: Strandbeests make the wind visible as walking, and their generations show how iteration itself can be the artwork.
creators.role_zh: 动态艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家，自 1990 年起不断“进化”Strandbeest：用 PVC 管制成、靠风力行走、在荷兰海滩上游荡的“海滩生物”。
creators.why_zh: 海滩生物把风变成了可见的行走，而它们的一代代更迭说明迭代本身就可以是作品。

creators.name: Ugo Rondinone
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Swiss artist who stacks huge boulders into colourful totems, most famously Seven Magic Mountains in the Nevada desert, and places stone giants in city plazas.
creators.why: His bright stacks against the desert show how colour and contrast alone make a virtual-feeling object in a real landscape.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 瑞士艺术家，把巨石叠成色彩鲜艳的图腾，最著名的是内华达沙漠中的《Seven Magic Mountains》，也在城市广场上安放石头巨人。
creators.why_zh: 他在沙漠中的鲜艳石柱说明，只靠色彩和对比就能让真实风景中的物体产生“虚拟感”。

creators.name: Florentijn Hofman
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Dutch artist of giant public sculptures of familiar toys and animals, above all the Rubber Duck that has floated in more than twenty harbours.
creators.why: His giant, cute objects in harbours are the physical version of the most viral AR move: take something small and familiar and make it huge in a real place.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家，把熟悉的玩具和动物放大成巨型公共雕塑，最著名的是在二十多个港口漂浮过的《Rubber Duck》。
creators.why_zh: 他在港口放置的巨大可爱物体，正是最容易走红的 AR 手法的实体版：把熟悉的小东西放大到真实场景里。

creators.name: JR
creators.role: Photographer and street artist
creators.bio: French artist who pastes giant black-and-white photographs onto buildings, walls, rooftops and landscapes, and builds huge scaffolded figures and anamorphic collages.
creators.why: He shows how an image scaled to a place, and seen from the right point, can rewrite a building or a border, the core move of world-scale AR.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师、街头艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，把巨大的黑白照片贴在建筑、墙面、屋顶和风景上，也用脚手架搭建巨人形象和变形拼贴。
creators.why_zh: 他展示了：一张按场地放大、从正确位置观看的图像可以改写一栋建筑或一条边界，这是世界尺度 AR 的核心手法。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 纽约，美国

creators.name: Jason deCaires Taylor
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: British sculptor who sinks cast human figures to the sea floor, where they become artificial reefs slowly overgrown by coral and algae.
creators.why: His underwater figures are an art work that nature keeps editing, a model for AR content that changes with its environment over time.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 英国雕塑家，把人体翻模雕塑沉入海底，让它们成为人工礁石，慢慢被珊瑚和藻类覆盖。
creators.why_zh: 他的水下人像是一件由自然不断改写的作品，是随环境长期变化的 AR 内容的范本。

creators.name: Patrick Dougherty
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: American artist who weaves saplings and sticks into huge swirling huts and towers on museum lawns and campuses, built with local volunteers in about three weeks.
creators.why: His stickworks feel like drawings made in 3D space, an analogue reference for volumetric AR sketching.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，用树苗和枝条编织出巨大的漩涡状小屋和塔楼，通常与当地志愿者在约三周内建在博物馆草坪或校园上。
creators.why_zh: 他的枝条作品就像在三维空间里画出的线条，是体积化 AR 绘画的模拟参考。
creators.based_zh: 教堂山，北卡罗来纳，美国

creators.name: Thomas Dambo
creators.role: Recycle artist
creators.bio: Danish artist who builds giant trolls from scrap wood and hides them in forests around the world, each with a story and a treasure-map trail.
creators.why: His trolls are the physical version of location-based AR games: characters hidden in nature, found by following clues.
creators.role_zh: 回收材料艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 丹麦艺术家，用回收木料建造巨型巨魔，把它们藏在世界各地的森林里，每一个都有自己的故事和寻宝地图。
creators.why_zh: 他的巨魔是位置型 AR 游戏的实体版：藏在自然里的角色，跟着线索才找得到。

creators.name: Isaac Cordal
creators.role: Street artist and sculptor
creators.bio: Spanish artist whose tiny cement figures of office workers and politicians (Cement Eclipses) are placed in gutters, on ledges and in puddles of cities worldwide.
creators.why: His miniatures show how scale and placement alone create a story in the street, a key idea for small AR figures on real surfaces.
creators.role_zh: 街头艺术家、雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 西班牙艺术家，他的小型水泥人偶（上班族、政客，系列名《Cement Eclipses》）被放在世界各地城市的排水沟、窗台和水洼里。
creators.why_zh: 他的小人说明，只靠尺度和摆放位置就能在街头讲故事，对在真实表面放置小型 AR 角色很关键。

creators.name: Slinkachu
creators.role: Street artist
creators.bio: British artist behind Little People, a long-running project that leaves hand-painted model-railway figures in London streets and photographs them in tiny scenes.
creators.why: He proves that the smallest possible intervention, found by attentive passers-by, can be a complete artwork.
creators.role_zh: 街头艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，长期项目《Little People》把手绘的火车模型小人留在伦敦街头，拍成微型场景。
creators.why_zh: 他证明了最小的介入，只要被细心的路人发现，也可以是完整的作品。

creators.name: Bruno Catalano
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: French sculptor whose bronze travellers (Les Voyageurs) are missing large parts of their bodies, so the harbour or street behind them shows through.
creators.why: His fragmented figures are a physical diminished-reality effect: the missing part is filled by the real world.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 法国雕塑家，他的青铜旅人系列《Les Voyageurs》身体缺失一大块，让背后的港口或街道透过来。
creators.why_zh: 他的残缺人像是一种实体的“削减现实”效果：缺失的部分由真实世界来填补。

creators.name: Mark Jenkins
creators.role: Street artist and sculptor
creators.bio: American artist who casts life-size figures in packing tape, dresses them and places them in streets in odd poses, provoking passers-by.
creators.why: His hyper-real figures test how people react to a body where it should not be, the same social test AR characters face.
creators.role_zh: 街头艺术家、雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，用封箱胶带翻制等身人像，给它们穿上衣服，以奇怪的姿势放在街头，引起路人反应。
creators.why_zh: 他的逼真人像测试了人们如何反应于“不该出现的身体”，这也是 AR 角色要面对的社会测试。

creators.name: Lorenzo Quinn
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: Italian sculptor known for giant hands that rise out of Venice's canals to hold up buildings or join across water.
creators.why: His hands turn a whole city into the context of one gesture, a clear idea for scale and storytelling in city AR.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 意大利雕塑家，以威尼斯运河中升起的巨手闻名，它们托住建筑或跨水相握。
creators.why_zh: 他的巨手让整座城市成为一个手势的背景，为城市 AR 的尺度与叙事提供了清晰思路。

creators.name: Alex Chinneck
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: British artist who makes buildings appear to melt, slide, float or unzip, using real bricks and engineering so the illusion holds in daylight.
creators.why: He does to real facades what AR filters promise to do, and shows how much the effect depends on exact, believable materials.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，让建筑看起来在融化、滑落、漂浮或拉开拉链，用真实的砖和工程手段让错觉在白天也成立。
creators.why_zh: 他对真实立面所做的，正是 AR 滤镜承诺要做的事，也说明效果有多依赖精确可信的材质。

creators.name: Tatzu Nishi
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Japanese artist who builds living rooms and hotel rooms around public monuments, so visitors meet a statue at eye level inside a domestic interior.
creators.why: He reframes a monument by changing the room around it, exactly what a portal or world-replacement AR effect does.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家，围绕公共纪念碑搭建客厅或酒店房间，让观众在家居室内与雕像平视相遇。
creators.why_zh: 他通过改变纪念碑周围的房间来重新框定它，这正是 AR 传送门或“替换世界”效果所做的事。
creators.based_zh: 柏林，德国 / 东京，日本

creators.name: Kurt Perschke
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: American artist behind the RedBall Project, a 4.6-metre red inflatable ball squeezed into alleys, arches and doorways of cities around the world since 2001.
creators.why: One simple object that reacts to each site's geometry is a perfect model for a spatial-mapping AR object.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，2001 年起开展 RedBall Project，把一个直径 4.6 米的红色充气球塞进世界各地城市的小巷、拱门和门洞。
creators.why_zh: 一个简单物体对每个场地的几何形状作出反应，是空间映射 AR 物体的完美范本。

creators.name: Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen
creators.role: Sculptors
creators.bio: Swedish-American Claes Oldenburg (1929–2022) and Dutch-American Coosje van Bruggen (1942–2009) made giant public sculptures of everyday objects such as a spoon, a clothespin and a shuttlecock.
creators.why: Their oversized objects are the original 'giant everyday thing in a park', a move AR creators repeat constantly.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家二人组
creators.bio_zh: 瑞典裔美国艺术家 Claes Oldenburg（1929–2022）与荷兰裔美国艺术家 Coosje van Bruggen（1942–2009），创作勺子、晾衣夹、羽毛球等日常物品的巨型公共雕塑。
creators.why_zh: 他们的巨型物件是“公园里的巨大日常物品”的原型，AR 创作者一直在重复这一手法。

creators.name: Richard Serra
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: American sculptor (1938–2024) of massive weathering-steel plates and curves, including East-West/West-East, four 15-metre plates across a Qatari desert.
creators.why: His work is about how a body measures space by walking, the same embodied scale sense AR has to respect.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 美国雕塑家（1938–2024），以巨大的耐候钢板和曲面著称，包括横跨卡塔尔沙漠、四块 15 米高钢板组成的《East-West/West-East》。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品关注身体如何通过行走来丈量空间，这正是 AR 必须尊重的身体尺度感。

creators.name: Isamu Noguchi
creators.role: Sculptor and landscape architect
creators.bio: Japanese-American artist (1904–1988) who treated whole landscapes as sculpture; his last work, Moerenuma Park in Sapporo, turned a landfill into a park of geometric hills.
creators.why: Moerenuma shows land shaped as a playable sculpture, a direct reference for designing AR in parks.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家、景观设计师
creators.bio_zh: 日裔美国艺术家（1904–1988），把整片风景当作雕塑；他的最后作品札幌 Moerenuma 公园把垃圾填埋场变成由几何山丘组成的公园。
creators.why_zh: Moerenuma 展示了被塑造成可玩雕塑的土地，是在公园里设计 AR 的直接参考。

creators.name: Fujiko Nakaya
creators.role: Fog artist
creators.bio: Japanese artist who since 1970 has made fog sculptures: timed clouds of pure water mist that roll over gardens, ponds and buildings and react to wind.
creators.why: Her fog is a real volumetric medium that people walk into and that the weather shapes, a benchmark for volumetric AR effects.
creators.role_zh: 雾艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家，自 1970 年起创作雾雕塑：按时间释放的纯水雾在花园、池塘和建筑上翻滚，并随风变化。
creators.why_zh: 她的雾是人可以走进去、由天气塑造的真实体积介质，是体积化 AR 效果的标杆。

creators.name: Amanda Parer
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Australian artist whose giant glowing inflatable rabbits (Intrude) sit in parks and squares, a comment on the rabbit plague in Australia.
creators.why: Giant soft animals in a city square are one of the easiest AR scenes to prototype, and her work shows how to add a message to them.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 澳大利亚艺术家，她的巨型发光充气兔子《Intrude》出现在公园和广场上，暗指澳大利亚的兔灾。
creators.why_zh: 城市广场上的巨型柔软动物是最容易做原型的 AR 场景之一，她的作品展示了如何为它们加上信息。

creators.name: Charles Pétillon
creators.role: Photographer and installation artist
creators.bio: French artist whose Invasions series fills houses, courtyards and landscapes with thousands of white balloons, including a 100,000-balloon heart in Covent Garden.
creators.why: His balloon clouds show how a mass of one simple element can re-map a familiar place.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师、装置艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，《Invasions》系列用成千上万只白色气球填满房屋、庭院和风景，包括伦敦 Covent Garden 中由十万只气球组成的“心脏”。
creators.why_zh: 他的气球云说明，一种简单元素的大量聚集就能重新映射一个熟悉的地方。

creators.name: Ana Mendieta
creators.role: Artist
creators.based: Iowa / New York, US (born Havana, Cuba)
creators.bio: Cuban-American artist (1948–1985) whose Silueta series pressed, burned and planted the outline of her body into earth, sand, mud and water.
creators.why: Her body-shaped traces show how a silhouette left in nature can carry presence after the person has gone.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 古巴裔美国艺术家（1948–1985），《Silueta》系列把她身体的轮廓压入、烧入或种进泥土、沙子、泥浆和水中。
creators.why_zh: 她留在自然中的人形痕迹说明，一个轮廓可以在人离开之后仍然承载“在场”。
creators.based_zh: 艾奥瓦 / 纽约，美国（生于古巴哈瓦那）

creators.name: Lita Albuquerque
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: American artist who places pigment, stones and spheres in deserts and ice fields to map the stars onto the ground, including Stellar Axis in Antarctica.
creators.why: Stellar Axis literally maps the sky onto the ground, a model for AR that links celestial data to a walkable site.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，在沙漠和冰原上摆放颜料、石头和球体，把星图映射到地面，包括南极的《Stellar Axis》。
creators.why_zh: 《Stellar Axis》真的把天空映射到了地面，是把天文数据与可行走场地相连的 AR 范本。

creators.name: herman de vries
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Dutch artist and former biologist who fences off small pieces of land as sanctuaries, letting nature grow undisturbed inside cities.
creators.why: His sanctuaries make an invisible process (wild growth) the whole work, marked only by a boundary.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家，曾是生物学家，他把小块土地围起来作为“圣所”，让自然在城市中不受干扰地生长。
creators.why_zh: 他的圣所让一个看不见的过程（野生生长）成为作品的全部，只用一道边界来标记。

creators.name: Hamish Fulton
creators.role: Walking artist
creators.bio: British artist who defines his art as walking; he records long walks in text and photographs and leads slow group walks in cities.
creators.why: His group walks show that a shared rule for moving through a place can be the whole artwork, useful for location-based AR scores.
creators.role_zh: 行走艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，把行走定义为自己的艺术；用文字和照片记录长途行走，也在城市中带领缓慢的集体行走。
creators.why_zh: 他的集体行走说明，一条共同的移动规则就可以是整件作品，对位置型 AR 的“行动乐谱”很有用。

creators.name: Spencer Byles
creators.role: Forest sculptor
creators.bio: British artist who spends a year at a time in a forest, building large sculptures only from what he finds there and leaving them to decay.
creators.why: His hidden forest works are discovered by walking, like geo-anchored AR pieces off the main path.
creators.role_zh: 森林雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，每次在一片森林里待上一年，只用在那里找到的材料建造大型雕塑，然后任其腐朽。
creators.why_zh: 他藏在森林里的作品要靠行走去发现，就像偏离主路的地理锚定 AR 作品。

creators.name: Richard Shilling
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: British artist who makes ephemeral works from leaves, stones, ice and sticks outdoors, photographs and films them, and teaches land art workshops.
creators.why: His colour-sorted leaves and balanced stones are small, fast pieces that map well to quick AR sketching exercises.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，在户外用树叶、石头、冰和树枝创作短暂作品，拍照和拍摄记录，并开设大地艺术工作坊。
creators.why_zh: 他按颜色排列的树叶和平衡的石头是小而快的作品，很适合改编成快速 AR 草图练习。

creators.name: Jon Foreman
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: Welsh artist (Sculpt the World) who arranges beach stones by size and colour into spirals and circles before the tide returns.
creators.why: His sorted stones show how order imposed on natural materials instantly reads as intention, a trick for AR layouts too.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 威尔士艺术家（Sculpt the World），在潮水回来之前，把海滩上的石头按大小和颜色排成螺旋和圆圈。
creators.why_zh: 他排列的石头说明，给自然材料施加秩序会立刻被读成“有意为之”，这也是 AR 布局的技巧。
creators.based_zh: 彭布罗克郡，威尔士，英国

creators.name: Choi Jeong-hwa (최정화)
creators.role: Artist and designer
creators.bio: South Korean artist known for colourful installations of cheap plastic objects and giant inflatable flowers and fruit that breathe in public squares.
creators.why: His breathing lotus shows how one slow, looping motion can make an object feel alive in a plaza.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、设计师
creators.bio_zh: 韩国艺术家，以廉价塑料物件组成的彩色装置和在公共广场上“呼吸”的巨型充气花果闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他会呼吸的莲花说明，一个缓慢循环的动作就能让广场上的物体显得有生命。

creators.name: Niki de Saint Phalle
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: French-American artist (1930–2002) who built the Tarot Garden in Tuscany, a hillside of giant mosaic-covered figures based on tarot cards.
creators.why: Her garden is a walkable world of characters placed in a real landscape, the dream of many AR theme parks.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 法裔美国艺术家（1930–2002），在托斯卡纳建造了《Tarot Garden》，一片布满以塔罗牌为原型的巨型马赛克人像的山坡。
creators.why_zh: 她的花园是一个把角色放进真实风景、可以漫步其中的世界，正是许多 AR 主题乐园的梦想。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 托斯卡纳，意大利

creators.name: Louise Bourgeois
creators.role: Sculptor
creators.bio: French-American artist (1911–2010) whose giant steel spider Maman, over nine metres tall, stands in plazas in Ottawa, Bilbao, Tokyo and elsewhere.
creators.why: Maman shows how a single giant creature with emotional meaning can dominate and protect a public space.
creators.role_zh: 雕塑家
creators.bio_zh: 法裔美国艺术家（1911–2010），她高逾九米的钢制巨蛛《Maman》矗立在渥太华、毕尔巴鄂、东京等地的广场上。
creators.why_zh: 《Maman》说明一个带有情感意义的巨大生物可以主宰并守护一个公共空间。
creators.based_zh: 纽约，美国（生于法国巴黎）

creators.name: Jeff Koons
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: American artist known for balloon-animal sculptures and Puppy, a 12-metre West Highland terrier covered in living flowers outside the Guggenheim Bilbao.
creators.why: Puppy is a living, seasonal surface on a giant figure, a reference for AR objects whose materials change over time.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以气球动物雕塑和《Puppy》闻名，后者是古根海姆毕尔巴鄂美术馆门外一只高 12 米、覆满鲜花的西高地白㹴。
creators.why_zh: 《Puppy》是巨型形象上一层会随季节变化的活表面，是材质随时间变化的 AR 物体的参考。

creators.name: Yinka Shonibare
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: British-Nigerian artist whose sculptures use Dutch wax-print fabric to question colonial history, including Nelson's Ship in a Bottle on Trafalgar Square's Fourth Plinth.
creators.why: He answers a historic monument with a new object on a plinth, the same gesture as AR counter-monuments.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 英国-尼日利亚艺术家，用荷兰蜡染布料质疑殖民历史，代表作包括伦敦特拉法加广场“第四基座”上的《Nelson's Ship in a Bottle》。
creators.why_zh: 他用基座上的一个新物体回应历史纪念碑，与 AR“反纪念碑”的手法相同。

creators.name: Tadashi Kawamata (川俣正)
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: Japanese artist who attaches hut-like structures of scrap wood to buildings, trees and bridges, as if a second, informal city were growing on the first.
creators.why: His tree huts cling to real surfaces, the physical analogue of AR content anchored to building facades.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 日本艺术家，用废旧木材在建筑、树木和桥梁上搭建小屋般的结构，仿佛第二座非正式的城市正在第一座城市上生长。
creators.why_zh: 他的树屋依附在真实表面上，是锚定在建筑立面上的 AR 内容的实体类比。
creators.based_zh: 巴黎，法国 / 东京，日本

creators.name: Marinus Boezem
creators.role: Conceptual artist
creators.bio: Dutch conceptual artist whose Green Cathedral in Flevoland (1987–1996) is 178 poplars planted in the exact floor plan of Reims Cathedral.
creators.why: A building drawn with living trees is a perfect example of an invisible architecture overlaid on land.
creators.role_zh: 观念艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰观念艺术家，他在弗莱福兰的《Green Cathedral》（1987–1996）用 178 棵杨树按兰斯大教堂的平面图种植而成。
creators.why_zh: 用活树“画”出的建筑，是在土地上叠加一座看不见的建筑的完美例子。

creators.name: Ackroyd & Harvey (Heather Ackroyd and Dan Harvey)
creators.role: Artist duo
creators.bio: British duo who project photographic negatives onto growing grass so that chlorophyll prints the image, and cover buildings and ships with living grass.
creators.why: Their grass photographs use light as a slow printer on a living surface, a poetic cousin of projection AR.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家二人组
creators.bio_zh: 英国二人组，把照片底片投射到正在生长的草上，让叶绿素“印”出图像，也用活草覆盖建筑和船只。
creators.why_zh: 他们的草地照片把光当作在活表面上缓慢打印的工具，是投影 AR 的诗意近亲。

creators.name: Cornelia Konrads
creators.role: Land artist
creators.bio: German artist whose site-specific installations make stones, sticks and fences appear to float, fly apart or dissolve in forests and gardens.
creators.why: Her 'frozen explosions' of natural material look like a paused simulation, an easy bridge to AR physics effects.
creators.role_zh: 大地艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家，她的场域装置让石头、树枝和栅栏在森林和花园中看起来像在漂浮、飞散或消解。
creators.why_zh: 她用自然材料制造的“凝固爆炸”看起来像暂停的模拟，是通往 AR 物理效果的便捷桥梁。

creators.name: Sam Van Aken
creators.role: Artist
creators.bio: American artist who grafts up to 40 varieties of stone fruit onto one tree, so it blossoms in many colours in spring.
creators.why: The Tree of 40 Fruit is a living, time-based artwork that reveals its design only in one season.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，把多达 40 个品种的核果嫁接到同一棵树上，让它在春天开出多种颜色的花。
creators.why_zh: 《Tree of 40 Fruit》是一件活的、基于时间的作品，只在一个季节里显露其设计。

creators.name: Dennis Hlynsky
creators.role: Video artist and educator
creators.bio: American artist and RISD professor who processes ordinary video of birds and insects so each animal leaves a trail, revealing flocking patterns.
creators.why: His frame-accumulation videos are the simplest demo of motion trails on real footage, directly transferable to AR camera effects.
creators.role_zh: 影像艺术家、教育者
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家、罗德岛设计学院教授，处理普通的鸟类和昆虫视频，让每只动物都留下轨迹，揭示群体飞行的图案。
creators.why_zh: 他的帧累积视频是在真实画面上叠加运动轨迹的最简单示范，可以直接迁移到 AR 相机特效。
creators.based_zh: 普罗维登斯，罗得岛，美国

creators.name: Stephen Orlando
creators.role: Photographer
creators.bio: Canadian engineer-photographer whose Motion Exposure series attaches colour-changing LED sticks to paddles, swimmers and athletes to draw their motion in long exposures.
creators.why: His colour-coded light trails show time as colour along a path, a precise visual grammar for AR motion trails.
creators.role_zh: 摄影师
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大工程师兼摄影师，《Motion Exposure》系列把会变色的 LED 灯棒装在船桨、泳者和运动员身上，用长曝光画出他们的运动。
creators.why_zh: 他按时间编码颜色的光迹，把时间表现为路径上的颜色，是 AR 运动轨迹的精确视觉语法。

creators.name: 3hund (Friedrich van Schoor & Tarek Mawad) / Glowing Atoms
creators.role: Light and projection artists (projection mapping in nature)
creators.bio: 3hund was the label of German media artists Friedrich van Schoor and Tarek Mawad, known for projecting glowing plants, mushrooms and giant spiders onto forests, beaches and building windows. Van Schoor now works with Dorothee van Schoor as Glowing Atoms; the work has been shown at Nuit Blanche Paris 2015, Ars Electronica 2017 and TEDx Sydney 2015.
creators.why: They project straight onto untouched nature and ordinary windows, showing how little it takes to make the real world look enchanted.
creators.role_zh: 光与投影艺术家（在自然中做投影映射）
creators.bio_zh: 3hund 是德国媒体艺术家 Friedrich van Schoor 和 Tarek Mawad 的创作名号，以把发光的植物、蘑菇和巨型蜘蛛投射到森林、海滩和建筑窗户上而闻名。van Schoor 现在与 Dorothee van Schoor 以 Glowing Atoms 的名义继续创作，作品曾在 2015 年巴黎白夜、2017 年 Ars Electronica 和 2015 年 TEDx Sydney 展出。
creators.why_zh: 他们直接把影像投到未经改造的自然和普通窗户上，证明只需很少的手段就能让真实世界显得充满魔力。

creators.name: Tony Oursler
creators.role: Artist (video sculpture, projection on objects and faces)
creators.bio: American artist, born 1957, who since the early 1990s has projected videos of faces onto dolls, spheres, trees and clouds of smoke, turning inert things into talking figures he calls electronic effigies. His work is held by MoMA, SFMOMA and Tate, among others.
creators.why: Decades before face filters, Oursler showed that a projected face is enough to make any object feel alive and aware of you.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家（影像雕塑，把影像投射到物体和脸上）
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，生于 1957 年。自 1990 年代初起，他把人脸影像投射到玩偶、球体、树木和烟雾上，让没有生命的物体变成会说话的形象，他称之为“电子偶像”（electronic effigies）。MoMA、SFMOMA 和 Tate 等机构都收藏了他的作品。
creators.why_zh: 在人脸滤镜出现前几十年，Oursler 就证明了：只要投上一张脸，任何物体都会显得有生命、仿佛在注视你。

creators.name: Lemieux Pilon 4D Art (Michel Lemieux & Victor Pilon)
creators.role: Theatre company (multimedia and holographic stage)
creators.bio: Founded in 1983 by Michel Lemieux and Victor Pilon, 4D Art makes plays in which live actors share the stage with life-size virtual performers projected on transparent screens. Their productions include Anima, La Tempête, NORMAN and La Belle et la Bête, the Cirque du Soleil show Delirium, and the Cité Mémoire projections in Old Montreal.
creators.why: They have spent forty years staging the exact problem AR designers face: making a projected person believable next to a real one.
creators.role_zh: 剧团（多媒体与全息舞台）
creators.bio_zh: 4D Art 由 Michel Lemieux 和 Victor Pilon 于 1983 年创立，他们的戏剧让真人演员与投射在透明幕上的真人大小虚拟演员同台。代表作包括 Anima、La Tempête、NORMAN、La Belle et la Bête、太阳马戏团的 Delirium，以及蒙特利尔老城的 Cité Mémoire 投影。
creators.why_zh: 四十年来，他们在舞台上反复处理的正是 AR 设计师面对的难题：让投射出来的人站在真人旁边也令人信服。

creators.name: Onionlab
creators.role: Creative studio (projection mapping and audiovisual installations)
creators.bio: Barcelona studio working across projection mapping, music videos and immersive spaces. It is known for stereoscopic 3D mapping shows such as Diplopia and Axioma and for façade projections on the Museo del Prado and Madrid's Palacio de Cibeles.
creators.why: Onionlab pushes building projection into true stereo 3D, the same depth trick that headsets rely on.
creators.role_zh: 创意工作室（投影映射与视听装置）
creators.bio_zh: 巴塞罗那的工作室，作品横跨投影映射、音乐录像和沉浸式空间。代表作有立体 3D 投影映射演出 Diplopia 和 Axioma，以及在普拉多博物馆和马德里西贝莱斯宫立面上的投影。
creators.why_zh: Onionlab 把建筑投影推进到真正的立体 3D，用的正是头显所依赖的双眼视差原理。

creators.name: BARTKRESA studio (Bart Kresa)
creators.role: Projection designer; founder of BARTKRESA studio
creators.bio: Projection designer whose Los Angeles studio maps architecture, sculptures and live events, from Game of Thrones premieres on Frank Gehry's Walt Disney Concert Hall to the 360° projected sculpture Shogyo Mujo, shown at Burning Man, Adobe MAX and SIGGRAPH and later installed at AREA15 in Las Vegas.
creators.why: Kresa treats a white sculpture as a blank body that projection can dress in endless skins, a direct model for AR materials on real objects.
creators.role_zh: 投影设计师，BARTKRESA studio 创始人
creators.bio_zh: 投影设计师，他在洛杉矶的工作室为建筑、雕塑和现场活动做投影映射：从在弗兰克·盖里设计的迪士尼音乐厅上为《权力的游戏》首映做的投影，到 360° 投影雕塑 Shogyo Mujo（曾在 Burning Man、Adobe MAX 和 SIGGRAPH 展出，后来常驻拉斯维加斯 AREA15）。
creators.why_zh: Kresa 把白色雕塑当作一具空白的身体，用投影给它换上无数层皮肤，这正是在真实物体上叠加 AR 材质的直接范本。

creators.name: Obscura Digital
creators.role: Creative technology studio (monumental projection)
creators.bio: San Francisco studio, with Travis Threlkel as chief creative officer, that projected onto some of the world's most recognisable buildings, including the Guggenheim, the Sydney Opera House, the Empire State Building and St Peter's Basilica. The Madison Square Garden Company acquired it in 2017 to develop what became Sphere in Las Vegas.
creators.why: Obscura showed that an entire landmark can become a live, reactive screen, which is how city-scale AR thinks about architecture.
creators.role_zh: 创意科技工作室（巨型建筑投影）
creators.bio_zh: 旧金山的工作室，Travis Threlkel 任首席创意官，曾把影像投到世界上最知名的一批建筑上，包括古根海姆博物馆、悉尼歌剧院、帝国大厦和圣彼得大教堂。2017 年被麦迪逊广场花园公司收购，参与打造后来的拉斯维加斯 Sphere。
creators.why_zh: Obscura 证明了一整座地标都能变成实时、会回应的屏幕，这正是城市尺度 AR 看待建筑的方式。

creators.name: Yeast Culture
creators.role: Visual collective (live concert visuals and installations)
creators.bio: British collective that creates live visuals for classical concerts, bands and gallery installations and also directs concert films. Projects include visuals for Ludovico Einaudi at the Royal Albert Hall, Nitin Sawhney and Bernstein's Mass at the Royal Festival Hall, and a live motion-capture performance with cellist Matthew Barley and Centroid.
creators.why: They design images that answer musicians in real time, a model for sound- and motion-driven layers in shared AR.
creators.role_zh: 视觉创作团体（现场音乐会视觉与装置）
creators.bio_zh: 英国团体，为古典音乐会、乐队和画廊装置制作现场视觉，也执导音乐会影片。项目包括 Ludovico Einaudi 在皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅的演出视觉、为 Nitin Sawhney 和皇家节日音乐厅版伯恩斯坦《弥撒》制作的影像，以及与大提琴家 Matthew Barley 和 Centroid 合作的现场动作捕捉演出。
creators.why_zh: 他们设计的影像会实时回应音乐家，是多人共享 AR 中由声音和动作驱动的图层的范本。

creators.name: Maxin10sity
creators.role: Projection mapping studio (architectural mapping, sky mapping)
creators.bio: Hungarian studio led by art directors László Czigány and András Sass that maps some of the largest buildings in the world, from Bucharest's Palace of the Parliament to the Bolshoi Theatre, Karlsruhe Palace and the Treasury at Petra. It has won the Circle of Light, Genius Loci and Berlin Festival of Lights competitions.
creators.why: Maxin10sity shows how far a single, well-understood facade can be pushed: every window, column and cornice becomes a moving part of the story.
creators.role_zh: 投影映射工作室（建筑投影、天空映射）
creators.bio_zh: 匈牙利工作室，由艺术总监 László Czigány 和 András Sass 领导，曾在世界上最大的一批建筑上做投影：布加勒斯特议会宫、莫斯科大剧院、卡尔斯鲁厄宫和佩特拉古城的卡兹尼神殿。曾获 Circle of Light、Genius Loci 和柏林灯光节等比赛大奖。
creators.why_zh: Maxin10sity 展示了一面被读懂的立面能被推到多远：每扇窗、每根柱子、每道檐口都成了故事里会动的部件。

creators.name: Limelight (Viktor Vicsek & team)
creators.role: Projection mapping and light art studio
creators.bio: Hungarian studio co-founded by light artist Viktor Vicsek, active in building projection since the mid-2000s, from the 2006 anniversary projection on the Hungarian Parliament to festival pieces in Toruń, Melbourne and Lille. It also makes immersive rooms, LED sculptures and mapping on miniature models and wood reliefs.
creators.why: Limelight treats the scale of the surface as a design choice: the same mapping craft works on a parliament, a 1:40 model or a carved wooden panel.
creators.role_zh: 投影映射与光艺术工作室
creators.bio_zh: 由光艺术家 Viktor Vicsek 联合创立的匈牙利工作室，从 2000 年代中期开始做建筑投影：从 2006 年匈牙利议会大厦的纪念投影，到托伦、墨尔本和里尔等灯光节作品。他们也做沉浸式空间、LED 雕塑，以及投在微缩模型和木雕上的映射。
creators.why_zh: Limelight 把投影表面的尺度当作一个设计选择：同样的映射手艺，可以用在议会大厦、1:40 的模型，或一块雕刻的木板上。

creators.name: Paul Friedlander
creators.role: Kinetic light artist (former physicist)
creators.bio: British artist who trained in physics and has spent decades building kinetic light sculptures in which spinning strings, lit by rapidly changing coloured strobe light, form floating waves, spirals and 'cosmic' shapes. His work has appeared at the Phaeno Science Centre, light festivals in Jerusalem, Skopje and Vilnius, and music festivals such as Shambala.
creators.why: Friedlander makes volumetric images out of almost nothing: one moving string plus timed light, a physical version of a hologram.
creators.role_zh: 动态光艺术家（曾是物理学家）
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，学物理出身，几十年来一直在做动态光雕塑：高速旋转的弦在快速变换颜色的频闪光照射下，形成悬浮的波、螺旋和“宇宙”般的形状。作品曾出现在 Phaeno 科学中心、耶路撒冷、斯科普里和维尔纽斯的灯光节，以及 Shambala 等音乐节。
creators.why_zh: Friedlander 几乎用“无”来造出立体影像：一根转动的弦加上精确计时的光，就是一个实体版的全息图。

creators.name: Jenny Holzer
creators.role: Conceptual artist (text in public space, light projections, LED)
creators.bio: American artist who since the late 1970s has put language into public space, first as posters (Truisms), then as LED signs and, from the 1990s, as monumental xenon projections of poems and declassified documents on buildings, rivers and landscapes. She represented the US at the 1990 Venice Biennale.
creators.why: Holzer proves that plain text, placed at architectural scale in the right place, is enough to change how a whole city square feels.
creators.role_zh: 观念艺术家（公共空间文字、光投影、LED）
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，从 1970 年代末开始把文字放进公共空间：先是海报（《Truisms》），后来是 LED 字幕屏，1990 年代起又用氙灯把诗歌和解密文件巨幅投射到建筑、河流和山景上。她曾代表美国参加 1990 年威尼斯双年展。
creators.why_zh: Holzer 证明了：只要放在对的位置、用建筑的尺度呈现，纯文字就足以改变整个广场的气氛。

creators.name: Musion (Musion Eyeliner)
creators.role: Holographic projection company (Pepper's ghost stage systems)
creators.bio: British company behind the Musion Eyeliner system, a modern Pepper's ghost that reflects a projected video off a thin, tensioned foil angled across the stage so that people and cartoon characters seem to stand in the room. It staged the Gorillaz 'hologram' at the 2005 MTV Europe Music Awards and life-size speeches by Prince Charles and Richard Branson.
creators.why: Musion turned a Victorian theatre trick into the stage 'hologram', the most direct physical ancestor of a virtual person placed in a real room.
creators.role_zh: 全息投影公司（佩珀尔幻象舞台系统）
creators.bio_zh: 英国公司，开发了 Musion Eyeliner 系统：一种现代版的佩珀尔幻象，把投影画面反射到一张斜拉在舞台上、绷得很紧的薄膜上，让真人和卡通角色看起来就站在现场。他们在 2005 年 MTV 欧洲音乐大奖上呈现了 Gorillaz 的“全息”演出，也做过查尔斯王子和理查德·布兰森的真人大小“全息”演讲。
creators.why_zh: Musion 把维多利亚时代的剧场戏法变成了舞台“全息”，它是“把虚拟的人放进真实房间”最直接的实体祖先。

creators.name: Holotronica (Stuart Warren-Hill)
creators.role: Holographic effects studio and inventor of the Hologauze screen
creators.bio: London studio founded by audiovisual artist Stuart Warren-Hill (formerly of Hexstatic), known for Hologauze, a fine transparent mesh that catches projected light so images appear to float in mid-air in front of performers. Hologauze has been used in shows by Eric Prydz, Beyoncé and illusionists, and in Holotronica's own stereoscopic live sets.
creators.why: Holotronica shows how a nearly invisible layer in front of the stage creates the same 'floating content in space' feeling that AR headsets promise.
creators.role_zh: 全息效果工作室，Hologauze 屏幕的发明者
creators.bio_zh: 由视听艺术家 Stuart Warren-Hill（曾是 Hexstatic 成员）创立的伦敦工作室，以 Hologauze 著称：一种细密透明的网纱，能接住投影的光，让影像看起来悬浮在表演者前方的空中。Hologauze 曾用于 Eric Prydz、Beyoncé 和魔术师的演出，也用于 Holotronica 自己的立体现场表演。
creators.why_zh: Holotronica 说明了：舞台前一层几乎看不见的纱，就能制造出 AR 眼镜所承诺的那种“内容悬浮在空间里”的感觉。

creators.name: Olivier Ratsi
creators.role: Visual artist (AntiVJ label; projection and perspective installations)
creators.bio: French artist and member of the AntiVJ visual label whose installations question how we perceive space. His projects Deconstruction Time Again and Echolyse use projection, LEDs and physical frames to build shapes that only become whole, or fall apart, depending on where the viewer stands, as in Onion Skin, DELTΔ, Shape and Frame Perspective.
creators.why: Ratsi designs with the viewer's position as the main material, which is exactly the problem an AR designer solves with every anchor.
creators.role_zh: 视觉艺术家（AntiVJ 厂牌；投影与透视装置）
creators.bio_zh: 法国艺术家，AntiVJ 视觉厂牌成员，作品追问我们如何感知空间。他的系列 Deconstruction Time Again 和 Echolyse 用投影、LED 和实体框架搭出一些形状，这些形状会随观者站的位置而完整成形或碎裂开来，例如 Onion Skin、DELTΔ、Shape 和 Frame Perspective。
creators.why_zh: Ratsi 把观者的位置当作最主要的材料，而这正是 AR 设计师每放一个锚点都要解决的问题。

creators.name: Tobias Gremmler
creators.role: Media artist and designer (motion visualisation, stage visuals)
creators.bio: German media artist who has taught in Hong Kong and works between computation, motion capture and stage design. He created stage visuals for Björk's Cornucopia tour, virtual costume-actors for Chinese opera, media scenography for theatre by Tim Yip, and the widely shared Kung Fu Motion Visualization.
creators.why: Gremmler turns captured body motion into imaginary bodies and trails, a direct template for AR effects that grow out of a performer.
creators.role_zh: 媒体艺术家与设计师（动作可视化、舞台视觉）
creators.bio_zh: 德国媒体艺术家，曾在香港任教，游走于计算、动作捕捉和舞台设计之间。他为 Björk 的 Cornucopia 巡演创作了舞台视觉，为中国戏曲设计了虚拟“服装演员”，为叶锦添（Tim Yip）的剧场作品做媒体舞美，还创作了广为流传的 Kung Fu Motion Visualization。
creators.why_zh: Gremmler 把捕捉到的身体动作变成想象中的身体和轨迹，这正是“从表演者身上长出来”的 AR 特效的直接模板。

creators.name: Sila Sveta
creators.role: Multimedia production studio (projection mapping, stage shows, holographic performance)
creators.bio: Studio founded in Moscow in 2007 that grew from festival projection mapping into large stage shows, product launches, concert tours and ceremonies worldwide. Its work combines 3D mapping, live dancers, kinetic stages and holographic screens, from the 2011 MIGZ festival to the Levitation performances and a holographic Swan Lake.
creators.why: Sila Sveta is a master of mixing live bodies with projected copies, so the audience can no longer tell which one is real.
creators.role_zh: 多媒体制作工作室（投影映射、舞台演出、全息表演）
creators.based_zh: 莫斯科，俄罗斯 / 纽约，美国
creators.bio_zh: 2007 年在莫斯科成立的工作室，从灯光节上的投影映射起步，逐渐做到世界各地的大型舞台演出、产品发布、演唱会巡演和典礼。作品把 3D 映射、现场舞者、机械舞台和全息屏结合在一起，从 2011 年的 MIGZ 节，到 Levitation 系列表演和全息版《天鹅湖》。
creators.why_zh: Sila Sveta 擅长把真人和投影出来的分身混在一起，让观众分不清哪个才是真的。

creators.name: NuFormer
creators.role: Projection mapping studio
creators.bio: Dutch studio that was among the first to tour large-scale 3D video mapping on buildings for brands and cities around 2009–2012, from Frankfurt and Madrid to Yerevan and Tokyo. It later added live motion capture, interactive window projection and sky projection to its toolkit.
creators.why: NuFormer pushed building projection from a fixed film toward live, responsive content, the same step AR takes when an overlay starts reacting to people.
creators.role_zh: 投影映射工作室
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰工作室，2009 至 2012 年间最早在世界各地巡回做大型建筑 3D 投影映射的团队之一，项目从法兰克福、马德里一直做到埃里温和东京。后来又把实时动作捕捉、互动橱窗投影和天空投影加入了自己的手段。
creators.why_zh: NuFormer 把建筑投影从一段固定的影片推向实时、会回应的内容，这正是 AR 叠加开始对人做出反应时迈出的那一步。

creators.name: NAKED, INC. (Ryotaro Muramatsu)
creators.role: Creative company for projection mapping and immersive events
creators.bio: Tokyo creative company founded in 1997 and led by Ryotaro Muramatsu, known for large projection mapping shows on Tokyo Station, Tokyo Tower and historic shrines and castles. Its touring events FLOWERS BY NAKED and TOKYO ART CITY by NAKED turn projection into walk-in, participatory exhibitions.
creators.why: NAKED shows how projection can dress a whole city landmark or a night walk through a shrine, a model for AR experiences tied to real places and seasons.
creators.role_zh: 投影映射与沉浸式活动创意公司
creators.bio_zh: 1997 年成立的东京创意公司，由村松亮太郎（Ryotaro Muramatsu）领导，以东京站、东京塔以及神社、城堡上的大型投影映射演出闻名。旗下巡回活动 FLOWERS BY NAKED 和 TOKYO ART CITY by NAKED 把投影做成可以走进去、可以参与的展览。
creators.why_zh: NAKED 展示了投影如何装扮整座城市地标、如何点亮一次夜间参拜，这正是与真实地点和季节绑定的 AR 体验可以借鉴的样板。

creators.name: Amon Tobin — ISAM Live (with V Squared Labs, Vita Motus, Leviathan, Blasthaus)
creators.role: Electronic musician; ISAM Live audiovisual show
creators.bio: Brazilian electronic musician on Ninja Tune whose 2011 ISAM Live show placed him inside a sculpture of stacked cubes that became a projection-mapped stage. The show was designed with V Squared Labs, Vita Motus Design, Leviathan and Blasthaus and returned as ISAM Live 2.0 in 2012–2013.
creators.why: ISAM turned a concert stage into one mapped object with the performer hidden inside it, a clear precedent for AR stage sets that wrap around a live body.
creators.role_zh: 电子音乐人；ISAM Live 视听演出
creators.bio_zh: Ninja Tune 旗下的巴西电子音乐人。他 2011 年的 ISAM Live 演出让他坐在一组堆叠方块组成的雕塑里，整座雕塑被投影映射成舞台。演出由 V Squared Labs、Vita Motus Design、Leviathan 和 Blasthaus 共同设计，2012–2013 年又以 ISAM Live 2.0 版本巡演。
creators.why_zh: ISAM 把整个演唱会舞台变成一个被映射的物体，表演者藏身其中，这是包裹真人身体的 AR 舞台布景的清晰先例。

creators.name: enra (Nobuyuki Hanabusa)
creators.role: Performance group combining dance and projected motion graphics
creators.bio: Japanese performance group directed by Nobuyuki Hanabusa in which dancers, gymnasts and jugglers play in exact sync with motion graphics projected on the screen behind and around them. Pieces such as pleiades and FUMA-KAI became some of the most viewed stage-projection videos online.
creators.why: enra shows how perfectly timed virtual objects can feel physically caught, pushed and thrown by a live performer, the core illusion of any convincing AR interaction.
creators.role_zh: 结合舞蹈与投影动态图形的表演团体
creators.bio_zh: 由花房伸晃（Nobuyuki Hanabusa）执导的日本表演团体，舞者、体操和杂技演员与投在身后和周围屏幕上的动态图形精确同步地表演。pleiades、FUMA-KAI 等作品成为网上观看量最高的舞台投影视频之一。
creators.why_zh: enra 展示了时间精准的虚拟物体如何让人感觉真的被表演者接住、推开和抛出，这正是任何令人信服的 AR 互动的核心错觉。

creators.name: Hiroaki Umeda (S20)
creators.role: Choreographer, dancer and visual artist
creators.bio: Japanese choreographer who founded the company S20 in 2000 and designs sound, light and projected images for his own solo dances. His works, from while going to a condition to Holistic Strata at YCAM, place a single body inside fields of projected lines and particles that seem to push against it.
creators.why: Umeda treats projected light as a physical force acting on a dancer, which teaches AR designers how a digital field can make a body read differently.
creators.role_zh: 编舞家、舞者、视觉艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 日本编舞家梅田宏明，2000 年创立团体 S20，为自己的独舞亲自设计声音、灯光和投影影像。从 while going to a condition 到在 YCAM 创作的 Holistic Strata，他的作品把一个身体放进投影线条和粒子组成的场里，看起来像被这些光推挤。
creators.why_zh: 梅田宏明把投影的光当作作用在舞者身上的物理力量，让 AR 设计者看到数字场如何改变人们对身体的感知。

creators.name: Robert Lepage / Ex Machina
creators.role: Theatre director; multidisciplinary production company
creators.bio: Québec director Robert Lepage founded Ex Machina in 1994 to mix theatre, film, opera and new media. His productions use projection, mirrors and moving machines to turn a small set into many places, from The Far Side of the Moon to the Metropolitan Opera Ring cycle and the giant Image Mill projection on Québec's grain silos.
creators.why: Lepage makes one physical set become dozens of worlds through projection and transformation, the stage version of what AR does to a room.
creators.role_zh: 戏剧导演；跨领域制作公司
creators.bio_zh: 魁北克导演 Robert Lepage 于 1994 年创立 Ex Machina，融合戏剧、电影、歌剧与新媒体。他的作品用投影、镜子和会动的舞台机械，让一个小布景变成许多地方：从 The Far Side of the Moon，到大都会歌剧院的《尼伯龙根的指环》，再到投在魁北克粮仓上的巨型投影 Image Mill。
creators.why_zh: Lepage 用投影和变形让一套实体布景变成几十个世界，这正是 AR 对房间所做事情的舞台版本。

creators.name: 1927 (Suzanne Andrade & Paul Barritt)
creators.role: Theatre company combining live performance and projected animation
creators.bio: London theatre company founded in 2005 by writer-director Suzanne Andrade and animator Paul Barritt. Its actors perform inside hand-drawn animated films projected onto flat screens, so painted doors, animals and crowds appear to share the stage with them; The Magic Flute with Barrie Kosky has toured opera houses worldwide.
creators.why: 1927 times real actors to drawn projections so precisely that the two worlds merge, a lesson in registration and timing for any AR story.
creators.role_zh: 结合现场表演与投影动画的剧团
creators.bio_zh: 2005 年由编剧兼导演 Suzanne Andrade 和动画师 Paul Barritt 在伦敦创立的剧团。演员在投到平面幕上的手绘动画里表演，画出来的门、动物和人群仿佛与他们同台；与 Barrie Kosky 合作的《魔笛》已在世界各地歌剧院巡演。
creators.why_zh: 1927 让真人演员与手绘投影的时间配合得天衣无缝，两个世界融为一体，这是任何 AR 叙事都需要学的对位与节奏课。

creators.name: Laterna Magika (Alfréd Radok & Josef Svoboda)
creators.role: Multimedia theatre (film projection combined with live performers)
creators.bio: Created by director Alfréd Radok and scenographer Josef Svoboda for the Czechoslovak pavilion at Expo 58 in Brussels, Laterna Magika mixed live dancers and actors with film projected on multiple moving screens. It became a permanent company of the Prague National Theatre and is often called the first multimedia theatre.
creators.why: Laterna Magika worked out in 1958 the core AR problem of timing a live body against a projected image so that the two seem to share one world.
creators.role_zh: 多媒体剧场（电影投影与现场表演者结合）
creators.bio_zh: 由导演 Alfréd Radok 和舞台美术家 Josef Svoboda 为 1958 年布鲁塞尔世博会捷克斯洛伐克馆创作，把现场舞者、演员与投在多块可移动银幕上的电影混在一起。后来成为布拉格国家剧院的常设剧团，常被称为世界上第一个多媒体剧场。
creators.why_zh: 早在 1958 年，Laterna Magika 就解决了 AR 的核心问题：让真人与投影影像在时间上严丝合缝，看起来像同处一个世界。

creators.name: Michael Naimark
creators.role: Media artist and researcher (projection, immersive film, VR)
creators.bio: Naimark worked at MIT's Architecture Machine Group (Aspen Moviemap), Atari Research, Apple and Interval Research, and later taught at NYU, USC and MIT Media Lab. His projection works from 1979 on, such as Displacements and Talking Head Projection, are early cases of projecting images back onto the real shapes they came from.
creators.why: Naimark's Displacements and Talking Head Projection are the direct ancestors of projection mapping and of face projection, and he wrote about them as research.
creators.role_zh: 媒体艺术家、研究者（投影、沉浸式电影、VR）
creators.bio_zh: Naimark 曾在 MIT 建筑机器小组（参与 Aspen Moviemap）、Atari Research、Apple 和 Interval Research 工作，后来在 NYU、USC 和 MIT Media Lab 任教。他从 1979 年开始的投影作品，如《Displacements》和《Talking Head Projection》，是把影像投回它原本来自的真实形体上的早期案例。
creators.why_zh: 《Displacements》和《Talking Head Projection》是投影映射与人脸投影的直系祖先，而且 Naimark 把它们当作研究写成了论文。

creators.name: Pierrick Sorin
creators.role: Video artist (optical theatres, Pepper's ghost, live compositing on stage)
creators.bio: French video artist known for self-filmed burlesque shorts and, since the 1990s, for 'théâtres optiques': small boxes where a filmed tiny Sorin appears among real objects through a Pepper's-ghost glass. He also designs video for opera, such as Rossini's La Pietra del paragone at the Théâtre du Châtelet.
creators.why: Sorin's optical theatres show, with a sheet of glass and a video monitor, how a virtual character can stand among real objects on a table.
creators.role_zh: 录像艺术家（光学剧场、佩珀尔幻象、舞台实时合成）
creators.bio_zh: 法国录像艺术家，以自拍的滑稽短片闻名；自 1990 年代起创作“光学剧场”：在小盒子里，通过一块佩珀尔幻象玻璃，让拍摄好的迷你 Sorin 出现在真实物件之间。他也为歌剧做影像设计，例如巴黎夏特莱剧院的罗西尼歌剧《La Pietra del paragone》。
creators.why_zh: Sorin 的光学剧场只用一块玻璃和一台显示器，就说明了虚拟角色如何站在桌上的真实物件中间。

creators.name: Dumb Type
creators.role: Artist collective (performance, installation, projection)
creators.bio: Founded in 1984 by students of Kyoto City University of Arts, including Teiji Furuhashi and Shiro Takatani, with sound by Ryoji Ikeda from the 1990s. Their performances pH, S/N, OR and memorandum stage bodies inside scanning light, projected text and data, and represented Japan at the Venice Biennale in 2022.
creators.why: Dumb Type turned the stage into a screen that scans, counts and overwrites the performers, which is exactly the relationship between a body and an AR interface.
creators.role_zh: 艺术团体（表演、装置、投影）
